Earlier, I unplugged my headphones out of my back panel in order to connect some speakers. The speakers did not work in the back panel, so I put them in the monitor and it worked fine.

Hi there. Just created my account, somewhat related to all the happenings this weekend at 'the other place', but also related to /r/bonsai over there and the general attitude. I hope that traffic picks up here and that more tolerance will be shown toward beginners and other.

To be honest, I am a beginner myself even having practiced for quite some time--as I take the point of view that few have truly mastered the art--and I never actually visited r/bonsai so I can't say. I certainly won't stand for abuse on a forum intended for peace and harmony with nature. I can promise you there will be no elitism.

I suppose I've been 'doing' bonsai for 20+ years, but that's because my first failed foray happened back in the 90s. My interest was rekindled here in Florida maybe 5 years ago, it turned into a full-fledged sickness until I toned it back down. Now I'm looking to get rid of trees to have reasonable amount of trees to maintain and develop.

Like with many things in life, we're all beginners to whatever degree. Even a seasoned bonsai master has things to learn, if they're receptive. There's quite a bit of elitism and cliquishness in the bonsai world, which can be found anywhere, but bonsai is slightly unique in that not all information can apply everywhere. So in many cases an explanation of a specific technique or some other bit of info is needed that many don't want to be bothered with. Many argue that it's a dying art form, and this mindset only serves to discourage newcomers.

I'm traffic will continue to trickle over here, people tend to stick with what they know, which is why Facebook is still a thing. But people will also go where they feel welcome.
